name: Cost per Equivalent Unit
description: Break down total production cost, and at advanced difficulty, spread it across equivalent units when some inventory is only partially finished.
formula: Total Cost = Direct Materials + Direct Labor + Manufacturing Overhead. At advanced difficulty, cost is spread across equivalent units: Equivalent Units = Units Completed + (Ending WIP Units × % Complete); Cost per Equivalent Unit = Total Cost / Equivalent Units.
business_contexts: a contract manufacturer combining raw materials spend with plant overhead for the year
a food processor totaling direct materials, labor, and overhead for a production run
an electronics assembler spreading total production cost across finished units and partially-assembled units still in process
a paint manufacturer computing cost per equivalent unit when a batch is only 60% complete at month end
a textile mill calculating cost per unit across finished goods and unfinished work-in-process
question_patterns: Once every direct and overhead cost is added up, what does it cost the client to produce this period's output?
What is the client's total production cost, once materials, labor, and overhead are combined?
What is the cost per equivalent unit, once partially-finished inventory is accounted for?
Given some units are still in process, what does each equivalent unit actually cost to produce?
solution_logic: Step 1: Calculate total cost = direct_materials + direct_labor + manufacturing_overhead
Step 1 (advanced): Calculate total cost = direct_materials + direct_labor + manufacturing_overhead
Step 2 (advanced): Calculate equivalent WIP units = ending_wip_units × pct_complete
Step 3 (advanced): Calculate equivalent units = units_completed + equivalent WIP units
Step 4 (advanced): Calculate cost per equivalent unit = total cost / equivalent units
key_insight: A partially-finished unit doesn't cost the same as a finished one — equivalent units convert incomplete work-in-process into the whole-unit terms cost per unit actually needs.
common_mistakes: Adding only one cost component and forgetting the others
Counting ending WIP units as full units instead of scaling them by percent complete
Dividing total cost by units completed alone, ignoring the equivalent units still in process
framework_soundbite: Total cost is materials plus labor plus overhead — and when some units aren't finished yet, spread that cost across equivalent units, not finished ones.
